req.err.no_sheet: No sheet has a Category and a Parameter column.

req.fix_tip: The AI assistant drafts the automatic fixes; nothing changes until you apply the card
req.help.1: How to fill in the requirements
req.help.10: Unit	The unit of a range (mm, cm, m, m2, m3) or, for the unit rule, the unit the value must use.
req.help.11: Rows	One row is one requirement. The first row names the columns; a title may stand above it.
req.help.12: Loading	A book with any refused cell does not load. Every refused cell is listed with its sheet, row and column.
req.help.13: Meaning	The check shows only whether the listed information is present and well-formed. Passing is not proof of code compliance.
req.help.14: Example	See the Example sheet for filled rows; it is never read as requirements.
req.help.2: Category	What the row is about: Doors, Windows, Walls, Rooms and more (the cell offers the list).
req.help.3: Level	Optional: only elements on this level, named as in the model.
req.help.4: Type	Optional: only elements of this type name.
req.help.5: Phase	Optional: only elements created in this phase.
req.help.6: Parameter	The parameter or field that must be filled, such as FireRating, width or Mark.
req.help.7: Required	yes: an empty value fails. no: only a filled value is checked. Blank means yes.
req.help.8: Rule	non-empty, one of, range, pattern or unit. Blank with no value means non-empty.
req.help.9: Value	one of: values separated by ; — range: 0.9..2.4, >=0.9 or ..2.4 — pattern: a regular expression the whole value must match.
req.line.not_run: {param}: not checked, the phase is not in this model
req.load_tip: Load a requirements workbook (.xlsx); it replaces the stored requirements
req.none: No requirements loaded. Download the template, fill it in and load it.
req.offer.export: The requirements report is ready to save as a workbook.
req.offer.title: {n} requirements read from {source}
req.template_tip: Save an empty requirements workbook with an example and instructions
req.title: Information requirements
